candidates: When adding new keyword parameters to `LAMMPSlib` or any other ASE calculator, use immutable types as default values: `()` for empty sequences and `None` for optional objects. Never use mutable containers such as `[]` or `{}` as defaults, since Python shares a single mutable object across all calls that use the default.

Enable ruff autoformatting on every new Python file added to the repository. The project is progressively migrating all source files to ruff as the standard formatter; new files must not be excluded from this tooling.

When extending an ASE calculator with an initialization extension point that depends on an external library object (e.g., a `lammps` instance that does not exist until first use), accept a user-supplied callback rather than calling specific named library functions directly in ASE code. For example, accept `initializer(lmp)` and call it once after the underlying object is created, instead of hard-coding calls like `activate_mliappy(lmp)`. This keeps ASE agnostic to the external library's Python API and avoids requiring ASE changes whenever the library adds new initialization functions.

Tests for generic extension mechanisms (such as `initializer` callbacks or `extra_cmd_args`) must use simple, self-contained dummy implementations that work with whatever build of the external library exists in CI. Do not call optional library-specific routines (e.g., mliap or kokkos initialization functions) in these tests, as doing so requires updating CI Docker images and creates ongoing infrastructure maintenance burden.

In `changelog.d/` entries, accurately reflect what problem each new feature solves and why a code change was required. If new ASE code was necessary because the relevant object or hook was not previously accessible to the user (e.g., the `lammps` instance is only created deep inside `calculate()`), the entry should make that clear rather than presenting the change as a minor or optional convenience.
